The mirror is sized consistently: M1/M2 are both 13.75/4.155 and M3/M4 are both 142.x/1.005, so each pair has ratio 1. The only inconsistent element is the gate of M4. It is tied to `iin`, the NMOS diode node at about 0.76 V, but to mirror the PMOS reference M3 it should be driven from `pd`, the node that M3 diode-connects. That wrong connection is the most likely fault. I haven't run a simulation to confirm it, so the ranking of the other two candidates is a judgment call.

```json
{"ranking": ["M4", "M3", "M2"], "fault": "Wrong gate connection on the PMOS output device M4: its gate is tied to iin (the NMOS diode node, ~0.76 V) instead of pd, the gate/drain node of the diode-connected PMOS reference M3. M4 therefore no longer mirrors M3's Vsg, which explains the large output-current error (49.6%) and the degraded output resistance. Fix: connect M4 gate to pd."}
```
